summary: Grenada has unusually rich official CBI data: Ministry of Finance quarterly CBI statistics (2014-2023, applications, approvals, new citizens and gross 'amounts due'), IMA quarterly statistics (2024-2026) and budget/MTFF documents with IMA revenue actuals and budgets, plus eight IMF reports (2014-2026). The main difficulty is definitions: government CBI revenue appears in at least four incompatible series (IMF fees-only 2019 vintage, IMF 2025 memo line, IMF 2026/MoF gross series, and MoF 'old' net format), and MoF gross 'amounts due' include money to developers. The 1997-2001 Economic Citizenship Program is documented only by a UN statement (suspension) and an industry blog.

events.title: Economic Citizenship Program made more attractive by 1997 amendment
events.description: Industry account: the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1997 underpinned an 'economic citizenship' (passport sale) scheme that ran until 2001. No primary document found.
events.quote: Grenada passed the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1997 was passed to make economic citizenship scheme more attractive

events.title: Grenada announces indefinite suspension of the Economic Citizenship Program
events.description: Foreign Minister Elvin Nimrod told the UN General Assembly that, after checking that no known terrorists had been granted citizenship, the programme was suspended indefinitely. An industry source dates the suspension to October 2001.
events.location: statement, section on fight against terrorism
events.quote: the Government of Grenada has taken a decision to suspend indefinitely, the Economic Citizenship Program.

events.title: Canada withdraws visa exemption for Grenada (reported)
events.description: Reported by an industry source (citing The Globe and Mail) as linked to passports issued under the Economic Citizenship Program. Primary source (Canada Gazette Part II, 19 Dec 2001) identified but not read.
events.quote: By Dec 2001, Canada revoked visa waiver agreement with Grenada citing security concerns with passports in circulation issued under Economic citizenship program

events.title: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Act No. 15 of 2013 passed
events.description: Parliament passed the Act establishing the current programme; regulations are SRO No. 17 of 2013. IMF describes the programme variously as launched in 2013 and 2014 (first applicants and receipts in 2014).
events.quote: The Citizenship by Investment Programme came into being in August 2013, when the Grenadian Parliament passed Act No. 15 of 2013

events.title: First citizen granted under the new CBI programme
events.description: IMF notes most early applicants were from China and the first new citizen was approved in August 2014; receipts began in September 2014.
events.quote: Most applicants to the Grenada's program so far originate from China, with the first new citizen from the program gained the Grenadian citizenship in August 2014.

events.title: IMF table: Grenadian passport visa-free to UK but not US, Canada or Schengen (2014)
events.description: IMF table of visa-free access for ECCU CBI countries (source VisaHQ) shows Grenada: US No, UK Yes, Canada No, Schengen No.
events.location: PDF p. 41, text table 'Visa-Free Access for Selected ECCU Countries'
events.quote: US              No         No        No        No

events.title: Bond restructuring gives creditors a share of CBI revenue
events.description: Agreement in principle with holders of the 2025 bonds included sharing of CBI receipts above US$15 million a year after the ECF programme; these 'Bondholder CBI-related payments' reached EC$78.4m in 2024 (IMF CR 26/9).
events.quote: The sharing of the CBI receipts will start only after the ECF-supported program and will exclude the first US$15 million in annual CBI revenue.

events.title: Cabinet mandates quarterly publication of CBI statistics
events.description: Prior action under the IMF ECF programme; the Ministry of Finance published quarterly CBI statistics from 2015 (replaced by IMA revenue statistics from 2024).
events.quote: A Cabinet conclusion mandating the publication of the CBI statistics has been approved in May 2015 (a prior action for the review).

events.title: EU-Grenada short-stay visa waiver applied provisionally
events.description: Grenadian citizens (including CBI citizens) gained visa-free short-stay access to the Schengen area.
events.quote: the Agreement has been signed and is applied on a provisional basis as from 28 May 2015.

events.title: Fiscal Responsibility Act requires 40% of NTF proceeds to be saved
events.description: IMF: first Caribbean CBI country to mandate saving CBI proceeds for disaster contingency. The current government later cut the set-aside to 10% and said none had actually been deposited before (2024 and 2025 budget statements).
events.quote: the FRA of 2015 requires that 40 percent of proceeds from the CBI program into the NTF are saved to make contingency financing available in the event of a ND.

events.title: ICSID accepts arbitration over CBI-financed Kimpton Kawana Bay resort
events.description: True Blue Development's case against the government concerns an unfinished CBI-approved project.
events.quote: In 2021, the ICSID accepted True Blue Development's request for arbitration with the government of Grenada over the construction of the Kimpton Kawana Bay Resort, which is a CBI approved project.

events.title: CFATF mutual evaluation flags CBI-related ML/TF risk understanding
events.description: IMF summarises the CFATF report's findings on weak understanding of risks associated with legal persons and the CBI programme.
events.quote: highlighted weaknesses in Grenada's understanding of the ML/TF risk associated with legal persons and the CBI program.

events.title: US law restricts E-2 treaty-investor visas for CBI citizens
events.description: People who gained citizenship through investment must be domiciled in Grenada for three years before E-2 eligibility (AMIGOS Act provisions). IMF dates the legislation February 2023; industry sources say it was enacted in the FY2023 NDAA signed 23 December 2022 - date to be verified against Public Law text.
events.quote: In February 2023, the U.S. passed legislation that requires people who earned Grenada citizenship through the CBI program to live in Grenada for three years before being eligible to apply for access to the U.S. through the E-2 investment visa.

events.title: US-Caribbean Roundtable on CBI in St Kitts
events.description: Led the five ECCU CBI countries to strengthen integrity and stop Russian/Belarusian applications (IMF CR 25/39 Box 1).
events.quote: comply with a request from the USA following the 25 February 2023 historic US-Caribbea[n] Roundtable

events.title: Grenada stops accepting Russian and Belarusian applications
events.description: IMF says processing of new applications was suspended in March 2023; NOW Grenada says applications stopped as of 1 April 2023. The resulting backlog was cleared in 2024 (MoF press release 2025).
events.quote: In March 2023, Grenada suspended processing new Russian and Belarusian applications.

events.title: CBI chairman says ~90% of 2023 approvals were Russian nationals
events.description: CBI Committee chairman Richard Duncan (interview) - claim, not official statistics. Same article reports Grenada's former ambassador to Russia removed from agents' list in March 2023.
events.quote: The overwhelming majority, maybe 90% of the applicants approved so far are in the area of Russian nationality

events.title: CBI Unit rebranded Investment Migration Agency (IMA)
events.quote: The Grenada Citizenship by Investment Unit was rebranded to the Investment Migration Agency (IMA) in March 2024.

events.title: Regional Memorandum of Agreement on common minimum pricing and a regional regulator
events.description: Grenada and four other ECCU CBI states signed an MoA after consultations with the EU; the EU later reported harmonisation at a US$200,000 minimum.
events.quote: In March 2024, following consultations with the EU, Grenada was among the signatories of a regional Memorandum of Agreement to establish, inter alia, common standards for minimum CBI pricing and a regional CBI regulator.

events.title: NTF minimum raised to US$235,000 and real-estate share minimum to US$270,000
events.description: SRO 12 of 2024 (gazetted 26 June 2024), corrected by SRO 15 of 2024. Previous NTF minimum US$150,000 (IMA website May 2024).
events.quote: These Regulations shall come into force on the first day of July 2024.

events.title: Transition deadline extended after Hurricane Beryl
events.description: Applications under the old prices accepted until 12 July 2024 (funds cleared by 31 July 2024).
events.quote: the Agency has decided to extend the application submission deadline to July 12, 2024.

events.title: Record CBI revenue from backlog clearance
events.description: IMA revenue 553.7m (new format), 97% above budget, attributed to backlog of Russian/Belarusian applications.
events.quote: extraordinary revenues collected in 2024, which resulted from a significant backlog of CBI applications—particularly from Russia and Belarus

events.title: 70% fee cut announced for local developers in CBI
events.description: Announced in the 2025 Budget Statement.
events.quote: this government in the coming weeks will pass amended regulations to reduce by 70% all fees that are to be paid by local Grenadian-developers

events.title: ECCU enacting legislation for regional regulator ECCIRA
events.description: Eastern Caribbean Citizenship by Investment Regulatory Authority to set and enforce uniform standards for programmes and agents; Grenada plans to repeal and replace its CBI Act in 2026 (Budget Statement 2026).
events.quote: the ECCU is enacting a common legislation to establish a new regional CBI regulator.

events.title: EU Commission: CBI schemes a potential ground for suspending visa-free travel
events.description: Eighth Visa Suspension Mechanism report names Grenada among five Eastern Caribbean countries; notes steps taken incl. harmonised US$200,000 minimum but continuing 'significant concern'.
events.quote: constitutes a potential ground for the suspension of visa-free travel under the revised Visa Suspension Mechanism.

programs.name: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Programme (Investment Migration Agency Grenada)
programs.notes: Legal basis: Grenada Citizenship by Investment Act No. 15 of 2013 and SRO 17 of 2013. First approvals 2014. Routes: NTF donation, approved real estate, significant investment (from 2024 statistics). Unit rebranded IMA in March 2024.

programs.name: Grenada Economic Citizenship Program (1997-2001)
programs.notes: Predecessor scheme; suspended indefinitely after 9/11 (UNGA statement Nov 2001). Details only from secondary/industry sources. Proposed as a separate program_id; merge into grd-cbi if the dataset prefers one id per jurisdiction.

new_indicators.name: CBI-funded contingency fund balance
new_indicators.definition: Balance of a government savings/contingency fund financed from CBI receipts (e.g. Grenada's 10% of NTF receipts held at the ECCB), at a date
new_indicators.notes: Stock, not flow; period is an as-of date

new_indicators.name: CBI real-estate investment inflows
new_indicators.definition: Money paid by CBI applicants into approved real-estate projects (e.g. developers' escrow accounts) in a period; not government revenue
new_indicators.notes: Complements cbi_fiscal_revenue; together roughly equal cbi_inflows

new_indicators.name: Applications processed
new_indicators.definition: Applications decided (approved plus denied) in a period, regardless of when filed
new_indicators.notes: Can exceed applications received when backlogs are cleared
